result.planSummary: Recovery story-implement run against the partial worktree left by the two provider-failure-terminated implementor sessions. Verified the Story 3 hard gate was already recorded in the team-impl-log (requeue patch landed; reason-class persistence proven). The partial worktree had already landed the production path (internal/sweep.ts classification table + report-walk/bucket/requeue/receipt, surface sweep op, compact default-on embed with sweep:false skip, CompactReceipt 'absent' placeholder flipped to SweepReceipt | {skipped:true}, shared receipt-schema fixture); I verified each piece against the owners' Epic 02 report/requeue contracts and the tech-design Flow 3 rules, then closed SV-03-002: wrote test/view-sweep.test.ts (10 tests: TC-3.1 five-state bucket/requeue/elapsed-bound/zero-provider, TC-3.2 once-per-invocation dedupe with work-row count by key, TC-3.3 shared-schema leg, TC-3.4 skip + background-poke heal + healed-form-in-view, blocked never-requeued, structural owner-noop via a turn pair sharing one work item, unclassified-code-is-permanent through the production terminal write path, classification-table unit legs, and the five-op zero-provider completion), amended the two stale placeholder assertions in view-pull/view-compact under the established sanctioned-amendment pattern (red-manifest re-recorded for those two files), and re-exported the classification table through test/fixtures (the boundary-exempt bridge). One test fix during the run: the heal leg initially drove the drain via a background status call, which is deliberately touch-suppressed (SV-01-PULL-STATUS-001); switched to running the default compact through a background SDK so the embedded requeue's poke-on-commit drives the production repair, which is the design's named path. Both gates green.

findingsFixed: SV-03-001 (critical): sweep production path was the Story 2 placeholder — closed; internal/sweep.ts + surface + compact embed verified against the owners' report/requeue contracts and Flow 3's bucket rules.

SV-03-002 (major): Story 3 test coverage absent and existing tests asserted placeholder behavior — closed; view-sweep.test.ts added and the two stale assertions amended with the red-manifest re-recorded.

TC-3.4 heal leg initially drove the drain via a background status call, which is touch-suppressed by design (SV-01-PULL-STATUS-001); rewritten to compact through a background SDK so the requeue's poke-on-commit drives the production repair path.
findingsSurfaced: If an owner requeue fails mid-walk, sweep returns the error and the receipt for already-committed requeues from that invocation is lost (each requeue is its own owner transaction, so they remain durable and the next sweep reports them in-flight). Receipt-level partial-failure accounting was not specified by the story; flagging for verifier awareness.

Default-on sweep means compact in manual mode now legitimately mutates derivation state (requeue rows) on a thread with transient failures; view-compact.test.ts's record-untouched assertions remain valid only because the file's first default compact performs the one requeue — noted in the amended test comment.

The runtime issue that forced this primitive-path recovery is recorded as lessons entry 6 in the team-impl-log: composed story-lead runs cannot recover from transient provider failures (resume returns the blocked package without redispatching, and the 51-turn partial session left no continuation handle).
